editions.title: AI is not a legal entity, so the solicitor stays accountable
editions.standfirst: The Law Society of England and Wales has reminded solicitors that AI is not a legal entity, which leaves responsibility for its output where it already sat.

editions.title: Research content is moving into the AI platforms, with claims attached
editions.standfirst: Midpage says its research costs a tenth of Westlaw and Lexis and now feeds Harvey; the price claim is its own and the terms are not stated.

editions.title: The gap at the top of UK law is widening
editions.standfirst: PwC's annual law firm survey, reported by Legal Futures, finds the top 100 firms still growing while the gap between the top 10 and the rest widens.

editions.title: Paying law firms for their emails puts privilege on the table
editions.standfirst: Above the Law reports that an unnamed technology company is paying law firms for access to their emails, and client privilege is the stake.

editions.title: Microsoft arrives in legal through the door lawyers already use
editions.standfirst: Microsoft has launched Copilot for Legal, according to Artificial Lawyer, and the stake is who owns the lawyer's desktop.

editions.title: Freshfields reportedly eyes outside capital for its AI unit
editions.standfirst: Legal Business, citing the Financial Times, reports that Freshfields is weighing external investment in its AI unit, and the stake is who ends up owning the tools a firm's lawyers rely on.

editions.title: Two legal AI rivals launch Intake; the name is the lesser point
editions.standfirst: Harvey and Legora each unveiled a product called Intake within hours of one another, and the buyer's question is what each does with the work it routes.

editions.title: The SRA asks what AI means for solicitor competence
editions.standfirst: The SRA has opened an eight week consultation on how technology and AI should shape solicitors' learning and development, with the Statement of Solicitor Competence in scope.
